title: C-01: Relay treats knowledge of tokenHash as machine identity — no proof-of-possession of the raw token at /control
evidence: relay/moch-relay-server.js:183-190 — registration validates only id shape, tokenHash shape, optional relay key; never the raw token
relay/moch-relay-server.js:192-203 — offline twin holding the same tokenHash is deleted ('re-pairing token hash from offline machine')
relay/moch-relay-server.js:146 — state.json reload restores tokenHash as the sole credential

preconditions: Attacker has read access to the relay state file (/root/.moch/relay-service/state.json on the VPS — root compromise, backup leak, or misconfigured perms) or any other hash disclosure, plus network reachability to /control. The legitimate machine must be offline for the takeover path (line 197 refuses a live holder).
reproduction_steps: On any host, open ws /control to the relay
Send {t:'register', machine:'m-x', tokenHash:<hash read from state.json>} — accepted unless the hash holder is live
Phone dials /api/ws?token=<real token>; relay routes the conn to the attacker's socket
detail: handleRegister authenticates a machine by tokenHash alone. Anyone who learns a machine's sha256(token) (the only value the relay persists in state.json) can register as that machine's id, or re-pair the hash away from a currently-offline legitimate machine (lines 192-203 explicitly delete the offline twin), then receive {t:'conn'} knocks and open /tunnel legs. They still cannot answer the phone's handshake (the home gateway would 401), but they occupy the machine slot, receive connection metadata, and can blackhole/DoS the pairing; combined with C-02's raw-token exposure paths any hash leak becomes a full machine-takeover primitive.
suggested_remediation: Require the raw token (or an HMAC over a server nonce) at /control registration, exactly as /tunnel already does; keep only the hash at rest.
limitations: Did not verify deployed VPS state.json permissions (out of scope, no network). Severity assumes hash confidentiality is the only barrier today.

title: C-02: Raw pairing token travels in relay URL query strings on both legs — lands in reverse-proxy access logs; 'relay never sees the token' comment is false
evidence: relay/moch-relay-server.js:308-312 — token taken from url.searchParams.get('token') before hashing
relay/moch-relay-server.js:377-381 — /tunnel?key=<raw token>
app/src/lib/gateway.ts:148-149 — token embedded in the WS dial URL (query string, not header)
app/src/lib/push.ts advertisement: push token also on the query string (gateway.ts:158)
moch-link/install.sh:222-223 — raw token as the tunnel-leg key in a URL
preconditions: Position: any reader of VPS logs (nginx access.log, journal) or the relay process memory/operator. No exploit needed — standing exposure by design of the URL transport.
reproduction_steps: nginx on the relay VPS logs GET /api/ws?token=… verbatim (default log format)
grep the access log → recover the pairing token → dial wss://api.moch.softland.tech/api/ws?token=… and speak JSON-RPC as the user
detail: The phone dials /api/ws?token=<raw pairing token> (app/src/lib/gateway.ts:149); the relay reads the raw token and hashes it locally (line 312), and moch-tunnel dials /tunnel/<id>?key=<raw token> (moch-link/install.sh:223). TLS terminates at nginx on the VPS, so the relay operator (and anyone reading nginx access logs, which by default log the full query string) obtains the raw gateway pairing token. That token IS the full session credential: with it one can dial /api/ws directly and drive the user's entire hermes gateway (sessions, transcripts, file r/w, exec approval flow) whenever the home machine is online. The header comments at relay:9-12 and install.sh:40-44 ('the relay never sees the pairing token, only its sha256') are incorrect.
suggested_remediation: Move the phone token to the X-Hermes-Session-Token header (already supported by the relay, line 305-309, and by the app's REST path) and have the WS client send it in a header too; send the tunnel key in a header as well. Fix the misleading comments.
limitations: Actual nginx log config not in repo — retention/disk exposure is an assumption of default config; mechanism (query-string transport) is fully traced.

title: C-03: Relay registration is open by default; unauthenticated /control sockets have no lifecycle cap
evidence: relay/moch-relay-server.js:61 — requireKey: '' default
relay/moch-relay-server.js:183-266 — no auth path when requireKey empty
relay/moch-relay-server.js:268-287 — connection handler sets no idle timeout for never-registering sockets
relay/moch-relay-server.js:433-436 — unauthenticated /health returns counts
relay/moch-relay-server.js:498 — server.listen(cfg.port) binds all interfaces (no host arg)

preconditions: Network reachability to the relay port. PROJECT.md puts the relay behind nginx on api.moch.softland.tech; if the raw port (9591) is firewalled and nginx only proxies specific paths, exposure shrinks accordingly — config not in repo.
reproduction_steps: Open N idle /control WebSocket connections; send nothing — none are ever reaped
Register 20 machines with random hashes from one IP; they persist across restarts via state.json
detail: --require-key defaults to empty (line 61), so any internet host that can reach the relay port may register up to --max-machines-per-ip (20) machines with arbitrary ids and arbitrary tokenHashes. Registration is permanent (persisted to state.json), enabling: (a) state.json pollution/persistence on the VPS; (b) socket-flooding /control before register — sockets that never register get no heartbeat and no timeout, so idle connections hold server resources indefinitely; (c) /health (line 433) leaks online-machine and live-connection counts unauthenticated. A remote attacker cannot evict another IP's machines (eviction at lines 217-227 is same-IP only), so impact is abuse-of-service and reconnaissance, not session hijack.
suggested_remediation: Default --require-key on (or auto-generate a key at deploy), add a register-timeout for unauthenticated control sockets, and gate /health counts behind the key.
limitations: Cannot verify live firewall/nginx path filtering from the repo.

title: C-04: Release builds silently fall back to the publicly tracked debug.keystore; the keystore itself is committed
evidence: app/android/app/build.gradle — release block: signingConfig keystorePropertiesFile.exists() ? signingConfigs.release : signingConfigs.debug
git ls-files — app/android/app/debug.keystore is tracked; passwords 'android' hardcoded in build.gradle
PROJECT.md:82-85 — local gradle release builds are the norm for testing
preconditions: A released/sideloaded APK actually signed by the debug key (v1.0.0 release signing not verifiable in-repo), plus attacker knowledge of the repo (public).
reproduction_steps: git clone the repo; assembleRelease with no keystore.properties → APK signed with the committed key
If a published APK shares that signature, adb install -r the malicious APK upgrades it in place
detail: signingConfigs.release is populated only when keystore.properties exists (gitignored); otherwise buildTypes.release signs with signingConfigs.debug, whose keystore is tracked in the repo at app/android/app/debug.keystore with the universal 'android' passwords. PROJECT.md documents local ./gradlew assembleRelease as the routine test path, and the GitHub-hosted v1.0.0 APK predates the EAS flow. If any distributed APK is signed with this key, anyone with the repo can build a malicious 'update' that Android installs over it (same signature → silent upgrade path with all permissions, including RECORD_AUDIO, SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW, and the embedded agent runtime).
suggested_remediation: Make release builds fail (not fall back) when keystore.properties is absent; remove debug.keystore from git or accept it for debug variant only.
limitations: Confidence medium because harm requires a debug-signed distributed build; no APK artifact was inspected.

title: C-05: usesCleartextTraffic=true app-wide, and pairing links default tls=0 — a crafted hermes://connect QR silently dials plaintext ws to a remote host with the token in the URL
evidence: AndroidManifest.xml:23 — android:usesCleartextTraffic="true"
app/src/lib/pairing.ts:37 — tlsRaw default '0'
app/src/lib/gateway.ts:559-561 — warn-only for plain ws:// to non-local host
app/src/lib/http.ts:5 — httpBase mirrors tls=false to http://
preconditions: User scans/accepts a pairing link whose host is off-device and tls omitted; attacker positioned on the network path (or running the named host).
reproduction_steps: Craft hermes://connect?host=<remote>&token=t (no tls param) as a QR
Victim scans and connects in a café Wi-Fi; attacker sniffs the ws frames and the token
detail: The manifest allows cleartext for the whole app. Pairing defaults to tls=false whenever the tls parameter is absent or not '1' (app/src/lib/pairing.ts:37-41), and the only guard for a non-local plaintext dial is a log warning (app/src/lib/gateway.ts:559-561) plus an unencrypted fetch path (http.ts:5). A malicious or mistyped pairing QR/link therefore pairs a remote host over plaintext — token and the entire chat stream (provider-key-gated model output, file contents, exec approvals) are readable by any on-path listener.
suggested_remediation: Default tls=1 for non-private addresses, or require an explicit user confirmation dialog before any non-local plaintext dial; scope cleartext to 127.0.0.1 via networkSecurityConfig.
limitations: Social-engineering precondition; no on-device test performed.

title: C-06: WebView debugging enabled process-wide in release builds — resident agent WebView holds browsing session, cookies readable over adb
evidence: app/src/components/AgentBrowserHost.tsx:53 — webviewDebuggingEnabled on the permanent offscreen WebView
app/android/.../BrowserRelayModule.kt:22,117-123 — process-wide setWebContentsDebuggingEnabled(true)

preconditions: Physical/adb access to the unlocked device (or a compromised adb chain). No root needed.

detail: AgentBrowserHost mounts an always-alive WebView with webviewDebuggingEnabled (and BrowserRelayModule.kt:117-123 calls WebView.setWebContentsDebuggingEnabled, documented there as process-wide). Functionally required for the CdpRelay/CDP toolchain, but release builds ship with WebView debugging on for EVERY WebView. Anyone with brief USB/adb access to the phone attaches chrome://inspect to the agent WebView and the gateway dashboard WebView and extracts cookies, logins, and page content — browserRelay.ts notes logins live in the WebView profile.
suggested_remediation: Gate setWebContentsDebuggingEnabled on BuildConfig.DEBUG when possible, or document the trade-off; consider a separate, non-debuggable WebView for any authenticated surface.
limitations: Design tension with the CDP feature acknowledged in BUILD-PLAN; no device test run.

title: C-07: Executable bootstrap artifacts (proot loader .deb, Ubuntu rootfs, QR renderer) downloaded with no checksum pinning
evidence: app/python-runtime/moch/linux_env.py:37,43,52 — TERMUX_BASE/PROOT_URL/ROOTFS_URLS, no sha256 anywhere in the file (grep: zero hashlib/checksum hits)
app/python-runtime/moch/linux_env.py:379-391 — _download writes bytes with no verification
moch-link/install.sh:22,1043-1044 — VENDOR_URL commit-pinned, curl -fsSL, no checksum
mitigating: _safe_extract/_check_member (linux_env.py:300-346) blocks path traversal and relative-symlink escapes in the rootfs

preconditions: Attacker controls the package repo/CDN response or holds a CA trusted by the device, at the moment of first bootstrap (or a pin change, which wipes and re-downloads, linux_env.py:519-528).
reproduction_steps: Serve a modified proot_*.deb at the pinned URL (or intercept TLS)
Victim runs Linux bootstrap; the swapped binary is chmod 0755 and exec'd per guest command inside the app UID
detail: First Linux bootstrap downloads proot_*.deb and libtalloc .deb from the Termux repo and the ubuntu-base tar.gz from cdimage.ubuntu.com over TLS, but verifies no hash (_download, linux_env.py:379, streams straight to disk; the stamp records only the URL). A compromised upstream, repo mirror, or any TLS-bypassing middlebox with a trusted CA yields arbitrary code: proot's loader is exec'd (via linker64) inside the app's UID on every guest command, and a malicious rootfs plants files the agent then executes. Same pattern in moch-link/install.sh:22,1044 — qrcodegen.py is fetched from raw.githubusercontent pinned only by commit hash.
suggested_remediation: Pin sha256 for the proot/libtalloc debs and the rootfs tarball; publish checksums for qrcodegen.py alongside the installer.
limitations: Standard supply-chain exposure; likelihood depends on upstream compromise, not app-side flaws.

title: C-09: CdpRelay loopback token compared with non-constant-time !=; token is 128-bit random and loopback-only

detail: segs.firstOrNull() != token is timing-sensitive, but the token is a fresh 122-bit UUID, the listener binds 127.0.0.1 only, and a cross-app timing oracle over loopback with a single boolean check is not practically exploitable at this entropy. limitations: None.

title: B-02: Always-on runtime runs as a dataSync foreground service with no onTimeout handling — 6-hour hard limit on Android 15+ devices
evidence: AndroidManifest.xml:39 — <service ... foregroundServiceType="dataSync"/>
HermesService.kt:207-208 — startForeground(NOTIFICATION_ID, notification, FOREGROUND_SERVICE_TYPE_DATA_SYNC)
HermesService.kt — grep: no onTimeout(short/int) override anywhere under app/android/app/src/main
reproduction_steps: On an Android 15+ device, keep the app alive with the foreground service across >6h cumulative runtime in a 24h window
Observe onTimeout -> unhandled -> ForegroundServiceDidNotStopInTimeException (logcat) and runtime death
detail: Manifest declares HermesService with android:foregroundServiceType="dataSync" (AndroidManifest.xml:39) and onStartCommand promotes it with FOREGROUND_SERVICE_TYPE_DATA_SYNC. On devices running Android 15 (API 35)+, dataSync FGS instances are capped at 6 hours per 24h: the system calls Service.onTimeout(int), and if the service does not stop itself the system throws ForegroundServiceDidNotStopInTimeException (process crash) after the grace period. HermesService has no onTimeout override, no type rotation, and the whole product premise ('Mochi is awake on this phone', START_STICKY automations) dies ~6h into every heavy day on those devices — taking the embedded gateway, cron-knocks watcher and FleetTurnQueue with it.
suggested_remediation: Override onTimeout(int) to stopSelf cleanly (and notify/persist), or move to a type without the 6h cap that Moch legitimately qualifies for (e.g. specialUse with a justification).
limitations: Docs/platform-behavior-based (Android 15 dataSync 6h limit), not reproduced on hardware here; applies only when running on API 35+ devices regardless of targetSdk.

title: B-03: HermesRuntime boot chain is single-shot and single-try: any gateway failure silently disables cron knocks for the whole process life
evidence: HermesRuntime.kt:28 — bootAttempted.compareAndSet(false, true) one-shot
HermesRuntime.kt:38-43 — gateway start precedes cron_knocks.start in the same try block
gateway_server.py:44-49,161-206 — start() waits up to _READY_TIMEOUT_S=90s; _port_accepts can race a foreign listener on the fixed port 9119
reproduction_steps: Hold 127.0.0.1:9119 open (or make start_server throw) before the app boots
Launch app; logcat shows 'python boot failed' once
Create an automation and let it run — it completes with no notification, permanently (until full process restart)
detail: HermesRuntime.start() guards with bootAttempted.compareAndSet(false,true) and runs selftest -> hermes_boot.boot -> gateway_server.start -> cron_knocks.start inside ONE try/catch that only logs. gateway_server.start blocks up to 90s waiting for the port and can raise (port 9119 occupied, start_server import failure, uvicorn bind error). If it raises — or if anything between selftest and cron_knocks throws — the catch logs 'python boot failed' and cron_knocks.start is never reached; bootAttempted stays true so no retry is possible until process death. Result: every automation completion is silent forever — the exact 'no knock' failure class the watcher was built for, with nothing in the UI distinguishing it.
suggested_remediation: Arm cron_knocks FIRST (it is independent of the gateway), and/or put each stage in its own try/catch; consider resetting bootAttempted on gateway failure so a later getGateway() can retry start().
limitations: Failure precondition is environment-dependent; the ordering fragility itself is unconditional.

title: B-07: linux_session.run timeout desynchronizes the persistent guest shell (orphaned sentinel/rc lines poison the next command)
evidence: linux_session.py:118 — wrapped command appends sentinel+rc after the payload
linux_session.py:141-142 — TimeoutError: return without proc.kill() (contrast :144-147 which kills on other exceptions)
linux_session.py:121-139 — next run() reads the leftover sentinel as its own
reproduction_steps: run('sleep 300', timeout_s=2) -> times out; immediately run('echo hello') -> output/exit belong to the dead command
detail: run() frames each command as '(cmd) ; echo SENTINEL ; echo rc'. On TimeoutError the branch returns {'ok':False,'error':'command timed out'} WITHOUT killing the shell: the previous payload keeps executing and its SENTINEL+rc lines arrive later, where the next run() reads them as the new command's output and exit code (garbage stdout, wrong exit status), and the new command is written while the old one still owns the shell. Other exception paths kill the shell for restart; the timeout path — the most likely one for long commands — does not.
suggested_remediation: On timeout, kill and null the shell (same as the generic exception path), or drain until sentinel before the next write.
limitations: In-tree callers are tests only today (terminal.py is a separate PTY path); severity held at low for that reason.

detail: The host's one-shot boot effect sets booted.current=true before await; if ensureBrowserRelay() rejects (transient native error, service not yet up at cold start) or resolves with st.running===false, ready stays false and the component returns null forever. The booted ref guarantees no retry on any later render/remount, and the failure is swallowed (.catch(() => {})) — browser tools stay dead until the user force-restarts the app, with no signal anywhere. The BUG-132 placement bug (early-return unmount) IS fixed — the host is child 0 in both _layout returns (_layout.tsx:263,290) — but the retry half of the chain has this silent permanent-give-up path.
suggested_remediation: Retry ensureBrowserRelay with backoff while !ready (or expose a retry tied to AppState foreground), and log/relay the failure instead of the empty catch.
limitations: Static trace; the concrete native failure modes that make the first call fail were not exercised.

title: G-06: Content-search hit rows in Chats always render '0 msgs' — constructed SessionRow omits message_count
evidence: app/app/(tabs)/sessions.tsx:124-132 — rows.push({...}) without message_count
app/app/(tabs)/sessions.tsx:306-311 — {item.message_count ?? 0} msgs
reproduction_steps: Chats tab, search a phrase that exists only inside message bodies
Result rows show '0 msgs'
detail: BUG-114's server content search maps each hit to a SessionRow carrying only id/title/preview/started_at/profile; message_count is never set, and the row renderer prints item.message_count ?? 0 + ' msgs' (line 308). Every server content hit displays '· 0 msgs' even for long conversations. Also these rows sort AFTER title matches by construction, which is fine, but the count mismatch reads as data loss to users.
suggested_remediation: Map message_count when the payload carries it and render '— msgs' when undefined, or omit the count for hit rows.
limitations: Assumes the /api/sessions/search payload may carry message_count; if it never does, hide the count for hit rows instead.

title: G-07: Settings -> Install Linux environment swallows all bootstrap errors (the BUG-016 pattern fixed in setup.tsx but not here)
evidence: app/app/(tabs)/settings.tsx:62-66 — no catch/error surface
app/app/setup.tsx:99-112 — same call is try/catch'd with setBootErr
reproduction_steps: Settings -> Install Linux environment with a doomed download
Row spinner stops, no error anywhere
detail: The install row runs void linuxBootstrap('ubuntu-24.04').finally(() => setBusy(false)) — no catch. linuxBootstrap rejects on failure (setup.tsx:99-112 catches its errors, proving the contract), so a failed download in Settings yields an unhandled rejection, the row flips back with no message, and the 60s status poll keeps stale data. Users installing from Settings get a dead button with zero feedback.
suggested_remediation: Catch and showAlert('Install failed', message), mirroring EnvStep in setup.tsx.
limitations: None.

title: G-08: Keyboard-avoidance mandated by AGENTS.md is missing on several input surfaces (plain ScrollView / no kbPad)
evidence: app/app/index.tsx:44 — ScrollView wrapping PairForm inputs (rule #3 requires KeyboardAwareScrollView)
app/app/add-computer.tsx:17 — same
app/app/setup.tsx:50 — same for the multi-step input wizard
app/app/bot.tsx:131 — ScrollView around TextInput edits
app/app/(tabs)/agent.tsx:212 — ScrollView; provider search + list, no kbPad
app/app/(tabs)/sessions.tsx:222-278 — search field + FlatList, no kbPad on the list container
reproduction_steps: Open Add a computer -> More options -> focus the token field with the keyboard up
On a small device the field/results sit behind the IME
detail: Per the repo's own rule (app/AGENTS.md, BUG-133), every input needs explicit JS-side avoidance because adjustResize is inert. These surfaces still use a plain RN ScrollView (not KeyboardAwareScrollView) with no kbPad on the list: index.tsx:44 + add-computer.tsx:17 (PairForm host/token/pairing-link inputs), setup.tsx:50 (wizard inputs incl. ProviderKeyForm), bot.tsx:131 (SOUL/desc inputs), agent.tsx:212 (provider search field with results below), sessions.tsx:222-244 / skills.tsx / connectors.tsx (top search fields whose result lists have no kbPad). On the forms the focused input can sit under the IME; on the search screens results are covered. Distinct mechanism from the tracked app-wide issue: these are uncovered surfaces lacking the mandated pattern.
suggested_remediation: Swap the form ScrollViews to react-native-keyboard-controller's KeyboardAwareScrollView, and add the kbPad list-container pattern to sessions/skills/agent/connectors search screens, per AGENTS.md patterns 3 and 4. Verify on-device per the rule.
limitations: Static audit only; actual occlusion depends on field position and device height — on-device verification required before triaging severity.

title: G-09: Reasoning-effort writes pass the raw active sid — a provisional (unsent) chat id goes to config.set and fails, though reads are guarded
evidence: app/app/(tabs)/agent.tsx:54 — provisional guard applied to reads only
app/app/(tabs)/agent.tsx:94 — applyReasoning({ ..., sessionId: sid }) — no guard, no ensureSession
app/app/(tabs)/agent.tsx:113 — rpc('config.set', { ..., ...(sid ? { session_id: sid } : {}) })
app/src/components/ModelPickerSheet.tsx:151 — the picker's apply path calls ensureSession() before config.set (the contrast)
reproduction_steps: Start a brand-new chat, immediately open Models (before first send), tap a reasoning-effort pill
Error alert 'Failed to save'; pill reverts
detail: refresh() deliberately skips session-scoped reads for provisional chats (BUG-013 guard, line 54), but setAndSave (line 94) and toggleReasoning (line 113) pass the raw sid into applyReasoning/config.set without the guard or an ensureSession() — unlike ModelPickerSheet.apply(), which resolves via ensureSession() first. On a brand-new chat whose session.create hasn't landed, tapping an effort pill (or flipping Show reasoning) sends config.set with a placeholder session_id -> gateway 'session not found' -> the optimistic pill snaps back with a failure alert, and the reasoning toggle silently reverts.
suggested_remediation: Apply the same provisional skip (fall back to scope 'global' or ensureSession({create:true})) in setAndSave/toggleReasoning.
limitations: Assumes the gateway rejects unknown session ids on config.set (as it does for session.title per BUG-006); not server-verified here.

title: G-10: Crew board: pull-to-refresh spinner can never show and offline renders as an indistinguishable empty board
evidence: app/app/(tabs)/crew.tsx:59-75 — refresh(): 'if (!online) return' before setErr; setLoading(false) but no setLoading(true) path after mount
app/app/(tabs)/crew.tsx:95-103 — 'loading && online ? spinner : FlatList' with RefreshControl refreshing={loading}
reproduction_steps: Load Crew once, pull to refresh — no spinner
Go offline, reopen Crew — board shows 'Read-only' hint with no offline/error state
detail: loading is set true only at mount; refresh() (also used as onRefresh) never re-sets it, and the RefreshControl is bound to loading — so pull-to-refresh silently updates (or fails) with no spinner. When offline, refresh() early-returns without setting err, so the board shows the stale/empty columns with the neutral 'read-only' hint and zero indication the data is dead — unlike every other screen which has an offline row.
suggested_remediation: Track a separate refreshing state for the RefreshControl (like sessions.tsx) and render an offline row when !online.

title: G-retry: AgentBrowserHost's resident WebView has no onRenderProcessGone/onError recovery — a killed renderer silently kills the agent's browser tab
evidence: AgentBrowserHost.tsx:50-69 no onRenderProcessGone/onError
MochiSurface.native.tsx:29-38 hazard+recovery documented
browser.tsx:267-269 visible tabs remount on renderer death
detail: Android kills background WebView renderers under memory pressure (hazard documented+handled in MochiSurface.native.tsx:29-38). The always-on host WebView handles neither callback — after renderer death the relay has no live tab while tools stay advertised: every browser verb returns 'No browser page...' until app restart. Browser screen's visible tabs DO handle it (browser.tsx:267-269).
